# <span id="aanchor417"></span> Configure Transaction Queue Imports

This feature requires the **Online Transaction Processing** module.

The Transaction Queue service allows FLOWCAL to provide a near-real time interface to SCADA systems and can be used as an alternative to file imports. This service permits a polling system to send information records to FLOWCAL one at a time, diminishing the need to save EFM data within the SCADA system and to write a “formal” CFX file.

Transaction Queue uses a Windows service (FcTrans.exe) and several database tables:

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>

<td class="TableStyle-FCtable-BodyB-Column-Standard1" style="vertical-align: top; padding-left: 5px; padding-right: 5px; padding-top: 5px; padding-bottom: 5px"><p>FC_TQ_MANAGER</p>
<p>FC_TQ_METER_CONFIG</p>
<p>FC_TQ_METER_EVENT</p>
<p>FC_TQ_METER_ALARM</p>
<p>FC_TQ_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES</p>
<p>FC_TQ_METER_BATCH_REPORT</p>

<td class="TableStyle-FCtable-BodyA-Column-Standard1" style="vertical-align: top; padding-left: 5px; padding-right: 5px; padding-top: 5px; padding-bottom: 5px"><p>FC_TRANSACTION_QUEUE</p>

SCADA systems, data polling engines, or third-party data collection solutions insert records that represent EFM periodic and batch flow data, source analysis, events, alarms, current configuration, and liquid tickets. The Transaction Queue service reads the records provided by SCADA systems and imports them into FLOWCAL. The data is fully validated and recalculated according to the settings in FLOWCAL.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Database Security">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Database Security</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Database Security">

The database security must be configured to allow the SCADA system to write transactions to the Transaction Queue tables.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="TQ Service">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Transaction Queue Service</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="TQ Service">

The Transaction Queue service is a Windows service that must be installed on the application server where FLOWCAL is installed. Depending on operation size (number of meters, locations, hardware specifications), customers may have multiple application servers, each server having the capacity to run one or more import services.

Running multiple import services allows FLOWCAL to distribute the work of importing data across multiple services instead of a single service.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

<div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example">

If a customer has 60,000 meters, instead of one service processing 60,000 meters on one server, they could run eight services across two servers (four on each server). Running multiple services would divide the workload by eight, so each service is handling no more than 7,500 meters at any time.

</div>

</div>

Once the Transaction Queue service is installed and configured, a Windows administrator can start the service.

<div class="procedure">

To run service:

1.  Click the Windows **Start** button.
2.  Type “Services” in the find field, and press **Enter**. This launches the Windows Services console.
3.  Scroll down the services list to find the Transaction Queue Service (FCSrvTrans.exe).
4.  Right-click the service name and select **Start**.

</div>

See: [All Services](../Settings%20Manager/Services/All%20Services.md)

</div>
